summary.en-US: Choose which languages each website gets. Overrides the Accept-Language header, navigator.language(s) in pages, frames and workers, and the JavaScript Intl locale. Supports *.domain wildcards and regular expressions.

description.en-US:
Firefox sends every website the same preferred languages. Language per Site lets you choose them per site: German for German shops, English for documentation, your own language everywhere else. How it works Rules are one line each: a site pattern and a comma-separated list of languages. example.com = en-GB, en, de only this exact host *.example.com = de, en the domain and all its subdomains /^shop\d+\.example\.com$/ = fr a regular expression on the hostname * = en-US, en every other site login.example.com = default no override, use Firefox's own setting The most specific rule wins: exact host, then regular expressions (first match from the top), then the longest *.domain, then *. Toolbar popup
  • See which languages the current tab gets, and which rule gives them.
  • Save a rule for the current site at any level: the exact host, the whole domain, or every site.
  • Edit, delete (with Undo) and drag to reorder all your rules.
Settings page
  • The same rule list, plus a tester: type a URL to see which rule matches and the exact Accept-Language header it sends.
  • Edit as text for bulk changes and comments, with per-line validation.
What gets overridden Not just the Accept-Language header. Sites can also read your languages from JavaScript, so the extension makes all of these agree:
  • The Accept-Language header on page loads, frames, images, scripts, fetch/XHR, WebSocket and worker requests. A header that a page sets itself on fetch/XHR is left alone.
  • navigator.language and navigator.languages in pages, iframes (including about:blank ones) and popups.
  • Dedicated, shared and service workers, including workers created from blob: and data: URLs.
  • The JavaScript default locale: Intl.DateTimeFormat, Intl.NumberFormat and the other Intl formatters, toLocaleString() on dates and numbers, localeCompare() and more. You can turn this part off.
Limitations
  • Things Firefox draws itself (date pickers, form validation messages, the PDF viewer) stay in Firefox's UI language. Extensions can't change them.
  • Changes apply to pages loaded after saving. Reload open tabs to update them.
Privacy The extension collects nothing and makes no network requests of its own. Your rules are stored locally in Firefox. The source code is on GitHub.

version.approval_notes:
Language per Site overrides the user's preferred languages per website.

No remote code, no minification, no build step: the package is the repository's manifest.json, src/ and icons/ zipped with `web-ext build`. Source: https://github.com/piit79/firefox-language-per-site

Why each permission and API is used:
- <all_urls>, webRequest, webRequestBlocking: onBeforeSendHeaders rewrites the Accept-Language request header on sites that have a rule (src/background.js).
- webRequest.filterResponseData: worker scripts (recognised by the Sec-Fetch-Dest: worker / sharedworker / serviceworker request header) get a small prelude prepended so navigator.languages and Intl inside the worker match the header. The prelude is the function installPatches from src/patch.js, serialised with Function.prototype.toString, followed by the language list as JSON. Nothing is fetched or generated from external input; any "use strict" directive prologue is kept first. Non-worker responses are never filtered.
- contentScripts.register: registers src/rules.js and src/content-isolated.js with the current settings embedded as `var LPS_CONFIG = <JSON>;` (JSON.stringify of the parsed rules). This is how the config reaches document_start synchronously, before any page script runs.
- MAIN-world content script (src/patch.js): wraps navigator.language(s), Intl constructors and toLocale* methods with Proxies. It receives its configuration from the isolated content script through a one-time CustomEvent handshake.
- storage: the rules text and one option, stored locally.

The extension makes no network requests of its own and collects no data (data_collection_permissions: none).

How to test:
1. Open the toolbar popup on https://httpbin.org/headers, choose "httpbin.org", enter "de-AT, de" and press Save.
2. Reload the page: the Accept-Language header shown is "de-AT,de;q=0.9".
3. In the web console, navigator.languages is ["de-AT", "de"] and new Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().locale is "de-AT".
4. Other sites keep Firefox's default languages.
